news.title: Morocco Women’s Team to Face Venezuela and France in World Cup Warm-Up Friendlies
news.lede: Rabat – Morocco’s women’s national football team will face Venezuela and France in two friendly matches on December 1 and December 5, respectively, as part of their preparations for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup. The Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) announced the fixtures in a statement published on its official website on Wednesday, confirming that both matches will serve as preparation for the tournament, which will take place in Brazil from June 24 to July 25, 2027. The match against France will take place at the Stade Auguste-Bonal in Sochaux, France, on December 5, with kick-off scheduled for 9:10 p.m. local time. Meanwhile, the FRMF has yet to announce the venue and kick-off time for Morocco's December 1 encounter against Venezuela.

news.title: Popa dilemma emerges, Ange impacted as boss breaks silence on Asian Cup’s fate
news.lede: The Socceroos’ quest for continental glory will likely be delayed by a year with the ongoing conflict in the Middle East set to postpone January’s Asian Cup. The tournament is due to kick off on January 7 in Saudi Arabia, but that plan is appearing unlikely to proceed following a pair of attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which left 14 dead and more than 300 injured. news.title: Pink Football Boots at World Cup 2026: Nike, adidas & PUMA
news.lede: The pink boot trend exploded at the 2026 World Cup: it was obvious from the very first team photo of Mexico vs. South Africa, where almost every player—including those on the bench—was wearing fluorescent pink or electric fuchsia boots. As the tournament progressed, players from other national teams appeared in the same colourways, almost as if the major suppliers had coordinated their efforts. There was a time when football boots came exclusively in black.

news.title: Gianni Infantino apologises to Fifa Council over World Cup sell-off plan
news.lede: Gianni Infantino has apologised to the Fifa Council on Friday about his failed attempt to sell off stakes in its competitions to private investors. But the president of Fifa also faced continuing questions about his role in the $4.2 billion Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme during a three-and-a-half-hour meeting in Zurich. Infantino was also asked to provide more information regarding the suspension of United States attacker Folarin Balogun's ban during this summer's World Cup in North America and the Fifa Peace Prize controversially awarded to US President Donald Trump. English and German football chiefs said they remained unconvinced Infantino was fit to ⁠continue as the head of football's world governing body.

news.title: Gianni Infantino: FIFA president apologises for World Cup sell-off plan - but FA and other European leaders still want him to resign
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has apologised for his World Cup sell-off plan at a three-hour FIFA Council meeting in Zurich on Thursday - and the Peace Prize he awarded to US President Donald Trump looks set to be ditched. Infantino's expression of regret for not telling the council about his plans earlier was not good enough for European football leaders, including FA chair Debbie Hewitt, who still want him to resign. UEFA wants Infantino to release all documents relating to the plan as they believe the 20 per cent stake in all future FIFA tournaments was being sold for a knockdown price.
